historical_reviews.deepseek: Close to the source query but grep-only output can hide errors and missing GPUs, and `reasonable` remains undefined.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Adds stable inventory, tool version, workload context, numeric range/units, timestamps and thermal/power/log correlation.
historical_reviews.related_cases: Power and stress cases can define operating context but cannot replace this row's per-GPU SCLK completeness.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Retains read-only scope and leaves numeric reasonableness to an approved project policy.

original_test_intent: Confirm SCLK telemetry is readable for every expected GPU and sensible for the explicitly identified workload/power state.
original_method: Collect complete ROCm clock output, map each SCLK reading to a stable GPU identity, preserve unit/timestamp/state and compare it to approved state-specific ranges.
manual_activity: Engineer supplies state-specific SCLK acceptance and resolves missing, stale or out-of-range readings before deciding the DUT verdict.
required_inputs: Expected GPU BDF inventory and device mapping
Collection workload/idle state and sampling window
SCLK units, expected range and transition policy
Power/temperature limits and protected evidence location
safety_requirements: Capture complete output and exit status rather than filtered lines
Stop on missing/duplicate GPU, unknown unit, invalid/stale value or driver/link/thermal/power error
Do not set clocks, power caps, workload or reset state
Preserve system logs and state context
agent_execution_scope: Map and parse SCLK for every expected BDF with unit, timestamp and state
Compare values only to supplied state-specific policy and correlate anomalies
Do not mutate GPU controls or decide PASS/FAIL
engineer_actions: Approve tool, inventory, state and SCLK range/transition rules

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The base query is applicable, but grep-only validation and unsafe transport can suppress missing-device and tool errors and provide no acceptance oracle.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Capture unfiltered `rocm-smi --showclocks` stdout/stderr/exit, then parse each approved GPU's SCLK with units, timestamp and known workload/power state.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: ROCm SCLK readability/reasonableness and source 5/5 timing are retained.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Generate a one-row-per-stable-BDF SCLK table with sample time, unit, workload/power state, approved range and discrepancy status.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the vague `reasonable` criterion measurable without introducing a clock mutation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Every GPU must be represented; a subset of grep matches is insufficient.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Dynamic clock policy can legitimately vary SCLK, so state and project thresholds are essential.

project_override_considerations: Project authority may define model- and state-specific SCLK ranges, but it may not reduce the check to mere output presence or authorize clock forcing implicitly.
expected_evidence: Expected GPU BDF map and collection state
Exact command, complete output, stderr, exit and timestamps
dmesg/syslog/SEL, anomaly disposition and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, procedure and Criteria consistently target SCLK readability/reasonableness; the undefined numeric policy is a supplyable acceptance input, not conflicting source intent.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Tool, inventory and range/state policy can be supplied; static review is complete and no missing package is treated as hardware failure.

review_improvement: Expands a grep hit into a complete stable-identity SCLK comparison with explicit units, operating context and non-mutating safety boundary.
independent_technical_reasoning: Modern GPUs adjust shader clocks by workload, thermal headroom and policy; one numeric sample is neither universally good nor bad. The defensible oracle is complete device coverage plus known state, units and approved envelope. Unfiltered output is necessary because a grep can retain valid-looking SCLK lines while hiding a tool error for another GPU.
